synthesis.overnight_summary: Gold extended its slide: spot fell 2.8% on Thursday and touched ~$4,011 in Asia, its lowest since July, as a $114 Brent spike from Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia kept Fed-hike fears alive and an AI/tech rout (Nasdaq -2.7%, Meta -7.5%) forced cross-asset liquidation. Unusually, gold fell even as US 10Y yields dropped ~15-19bp to ~4.95%, the dollar stayed near a 3-week low, and December hike odds slipped from ~90% to ~80%; safe-haven money went to Treasuries, the yen and the franc instead. Silver crashed ~5%. For MCX, the overnight COMEX drop of ~$28 from the close is partly offset by a weaker rupee (~95.09 offshore vs 94.83), giving a model fair open near Rs 142,707 (gap ~Rs -602). With spot about $19 above the key $4,000 level and momentum oversold, today's MCX session is likely to be a fight between continued liquidation and dip-buying/short-covering into the weekend.

At 08:59 IST compare the MCX pre-open with the fair 142,707: within +/-300 means the open is aligned and tradeable; a gap of more than 300 means wait 15-30 min for convergence.
